name: Bell 222 / 230 / 430
summary: A family of sleek twin-turbine Bell executive and EMS helicopters; the 222/230 have two-blade rotors, the later 430 has a four-blade bearingless rotor.

wings: Two-blade main rotor on the earlier models, four-blade rotor on the largest, stretched version
Sleek low mast fairing; the earliest model has small stub-wing sponsons
engines: Twin turboshafts side by side behind the cabin under a long smooth cowling
Exhaust stacks at the top rear of the cowl
fuselage: Smooth aerodynamic body with a long swept nose and a wide cabin with large windows
Undercarriage is either skids on faired legs or retractable wheels in sponsons, depending on model
tail: Slim boom with a swept vertical fin
Horizontal stabilizer with end plates and a two-blade tail rotor

tellTales: Sleek executive-style twin-turbine helicopter with a long smooth cowl
Long swept nose with a wide, large-windowed cabin
Either wheels retracting into stub sponsons or skids on faired legs, under a swept tailboom with end-plate stabilizers

confusedWith.howToTell: The 412 is a boxy utility helicopter with a squared-off nose and wide sliding doors; the 222/430 are smoother with a long swept nose.
The AW109 has a four-blade rotor and a more compact body with a different tail; the 222 has two blades and distinctive stub-wing sponsons, while the 430 is larger and uses skids.
The H135 has a ducted tail fan; the 222/430 have an open conventional tail rotor.
The 429 is a bit smaller and has larger sliding doors and a different cowl; the 430 has a longer cabin and a sleeker nose.
